title: cmate-orchestrate observe report v1
description: Report printed to stdout and written to observe-report.json by the post-merge observation runner (scripts/observe.mjs, Issue #221). Closed schema: an unknown field is a contract violation, not something a reader may ignore. It records measurements taken on the BASE BRANCH AFTER a merge — the ones no worktree can take — and it DOES NOT ADJUDICATE. There is no verdict field, no threshold and no acceptance vocabulary anywhere in this document: `status` reports how much of the requested collection actually happened, and the words `pass` and `fail` appear nowhere except inside a GitHub `conclusion`, which is transcribed verbatim and always sits under a key of that name. Three measured failures shaped it (Kewton/CommandMate#1835): the runs right after a merge are outliers, so every sample is listed and never only a median; a run's wall clock carries setup noise the criterion is not about, so a step can be measured on its own; and a defect appeared on the fifth run of five, so how many samples a number rests on is recorded next to it.

status.description: COMPLETENESS OF COLLECTION, and nothing else. success: every observation of every merged issue got the runs_requested samples that were asked for. partial: something was short, unobservable, or a requested comment did not land — the values that WERE collected are still in the report. refused: the invocation was not accepted and nothing was observed at all (issues is null). This enum deliberately carries no acceptance vocabulary: whether the numbers meet the issue's criterion is a reading a human makes, and five people reading one series can reach different conclusions (the measured case where four runs said the opposite of five).

runs_requested.description: The --runs value. Never defaulted by the runner: 3 runs and 8 runs of one workflow gave opposite answers about the same change, so the number is a decision the operator makes and this field records. 0 only in a refusal envelope.

max_wait_sec.description: The --max-wait budget in seconds. On reaching it the runner publishes what it has with status partial and an observation_incomplete limitation naming the shortfall; it never fills the gap in.

out_dir.description: Directory the observation artifacts were written to, REDACTED — unlike merge-report's out_dir, which is stored as given. This is the one report in the package designed to be published (--comment), so a host path that names somebody's home directory does not sit a byte away from a GitHub comment. The real directory is printed on stderr.

observations_source.description: WHERE the declaration came from, stated rather than inferred. plan: plan.profile.observations, the default and the same handoff dispatch_defaults and integration_baseline use — what runs is what the approved plan froze. profile_file: --profile named a profile on disk, which is the documented escape for a plan frozen before the profile declared observations (re-planning would derive a new run id, and the wave being observed has already merged). The second always raises the observations_from_profile_file limitation, because the two sources can differ.

observations_declared.description: The declarations that were collected, transcribed in profile order.

issues.description: One entry per merged target of the merge report, in merge order. null whenever the run refused its input — stated as data so a consumer cannot read 'we could not look' as 'we looked and there was nothing', the same distinction inspect.mjs's null inspection carries.

completion_check.description: The runner's self-report on its own discipline. The member is `satisfied`, not `passed`: nothing in this document adjudicates, and a field named after a verdict is how a verdict gets read into one.

summary_markdown.description: One table row per SAMPLE, never a median on its own. That is the whole point of the document: the retracted report this runner exists to prevent was a median read without the series under it. Under --comment --approve these are the exact bytes posted as an issue comment, which is why the summary is rendered before the comment is sent and never re-rendered after.

declaration.description: A declaration as lib.mjs normalizeObservations rebuilt it: id, kind, the kind's own keys, then unit. The kind's keys are validated at load time, so a declaration that reaches this report is one whose required keys are present.

merged_at.description: The instant the PR merged, read with `gh pr view <n> --json mergedAt,mergeCommit`. It is NOT in merge-report.v1 and never was — that report carries pr_number and merged: bool — so it is fetched here and written down here: an observation window whose start nobody recorded is an observation nobody can re-check. It is never approximated from the merge report's own timestamps; a window with an invented start attributes runs to a merge that did not cause them.

merge_commit.description: The merge commit oid from the same call. kind: command checks this exact commit out into a throwaway detached worktree, so the number it prints describes the state immediately after this issue landed rather than the branch tip at some later moment.

observable.description: False means the merge instant could not be read, so no window could be opened and NOTHING was collected for this issue (observations is empty and note says why, with a matching not_observable limitation). It is never rounded into an issue whose observations happened to be empty.

collected.description: How many samples were found at all. Equals samples.length.

counted.description: How many of them entered median and mean. collected minus counted is always accounted for in excluded.

complete.description: collected === requested. False is what makes the run partial, and it is stated rather than filled in.

samples.description: EVERY sample, in the order it was observed (oldest run first), excluded ones included. A median without its series is the shape of the retracted report this runner replaces.

excluded.description: The samples that did NOT enter the aggregate, tallied by why, in order of first appearance. A cancelled, unfinished or non-green run did not measure the thing, so it is left out of median and mean — but never left out silently.

baseline.description: The 'before' value, looked up by id in whatever document --inspect names. null means no --inspect was given, or that document holds no numeric value under this id — a fact about the artifact, not a defect in it. No producer's format is assumed: the rule is the first object a breadth-first walk of the document reaches that has this id and a finite number under value (preferred) or median.

baseline_source.description: Where in the --inspect document that number was found, as a slash path, so the match can be checked rather than trusted.

run_id.description: The GitHub Actions run id. null for kind: command, which has no run.

value.description: The measurement, in the observation's unit. null exactly when the sample was not counted.

counted.description: Whether this sample entered median and mean.

conclusion.description: The GitHub conclusion of the run or step, TRANSCRIBED VERBATIM — this is the only vocabulary in the whole document that is not this runner's own, which is why it always sits under a key of this name. Three values are the runner's instead, for facts GitHub has no word for: in_progress (the run or step has not concluded), and, for kind: command, ok / no_number_on_stdout / command_unavailable / jobs_unavailable / job_not_found / step_not_found.

comment.description: The only write this runner has (Issue #221), and the first path in this package that writes to GitHub at all: `gh issue comment`. --comment requires --approve, and the refusal happens before any input is read, so a mistyped invocation cannot post anything on its way to being rejected. It posts a COMMENT and never edits an issue body — SKILL.md section 1 puts automatic body editing out of scope and this does not move that line.

written.description: One entry per issue a comment was attempted on. Empty on every run that did not pass both flags, which is what 'nothing was written to GitHub' looks like.
